quest.title: Impromptu Poem of the Crimson Dawn
quest.description: You meet someone locked in a cage in the suburbs...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

dialogues.speaker: Composed-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: #Hi, {M#bro}{F#girl}.

dialogues.speaker: Vicious-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Today just isn't our day, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Composed-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Tough luck for us both.

dialogues.speaker: Vicious-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: I see that you're out for a stroll with your pet, but you walked right into our camp.

dialogues.speaker: Composed-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: You'll pay for that.

dialogues.speaker: Vicious-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: We were about to call it a day, but thanks to you, we've got more work to do!

dialogues.speaker: Composed-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Just our luck.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, what are we gonna do? We're being robbed!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're missing the point! First of all, Paimon is not a pet that needs to be taken for a walk!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever... You think you're the boss? Paimon'll show you how wrong you are. It's show time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We're the legendary {NICKNAME} and Paimon! It's your last chance, outlaws! Surrender now, or prepare to meet your end!

dialogues.speaker: Vicious-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Well, ain't that somethin'? A pet that talks! That could fetch a handsome sum on the market.

dialogues.speaker: Composed-Looking Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: A handsome sum indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehhhh!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Enough talk. Let's do this!

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: W—Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: Monsieur Havisham, Monsieur Jingle, I thought we had a deal! I promised to give you my goods, and in return, you wouldn't hurt any innocent people or animals in the interim.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: Hmm. Well, I suppose we've just met, so you probably haven't heard about our story. We used to be apprentices in the Court of Fontaine, but then we got kicked out. Do you know why?

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: They said we didn't work hard enough.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: But no matter what comes our way, my brother and I always learn from our failures. So we lost our job because we didn't work hard enough? Then we'll be sure to work harder than anyone else at our next gig!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I also work harder than most when it comes to fighting crime.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: #Hah, {M#bro}{F#girl}, I'll admit that you don't look like the typical hero, but you've got guts. If a fight's what you want, that's what you'll get!

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: I'll have you know that this isn't our first rodeo.

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: Please! Would you all just hold your horses and listen to me? What good will it bring to fight each other?

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: I would hate to see any of you get hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: You know what? I've got enough money for all of us. I'm not sure if it's sufficient for your services, but I'm willing to pay double the ransom if you lay down your weapons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: Thank you for asking. I do miss my usual freedom, but apart from that, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I thought they were the ones who locked you up! Then why don't you accept our help? Why are you offering them an even bigger ransom?

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: My dear friend, sometimes you may encounter difficulties in life that you cannot overcome by yourself. I believe Monsieur Havisham and Monsieur Jingle have found themselves in such a pickle.

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: I have the choice to save the lives of two people, or even four, all for the cost of a nigh nugatory sum of gold. Wouldn't you call that a fair deal?

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: And you needn't worry about me. I have reached an agreement with them.

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: In exchange for my freedom, I have offered to provide them with a batch of goods. This way, they will be furnished with a sufficient amount of capital to start a living that does not involve harming innocent people and animals.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: That's indeed what you said.

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: That's indeed what we heard.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: All that for someone you had never met... You have a heart of gold, my friend! I'm so touched.

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: #We are men of our word. We'll let you walk free today, lucky {M#bro}{F#girl} — and don't forget to take your pet with you!

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: #That's good! Alright, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you can both go home now!

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: No need to worry about me. I'll take Monsieurs Havisham and Jingle to retrieve the goods they have been promised — an easy task if I ever saw one.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The Treasure Hoarders free the redhead from his cage, and the three of them head east together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #They're gone... {NICKNAME}, do you really think the Treasure Hoarders are gonna let him go? He doesn't seem like the sharpest knife in the drawer.

choices.text: He could have paid me to fix the problem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He might be the sort of person who wouldn't even harm a fly. Paimon thought that lot only existed in fairy tales.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Paimon's dying to know what's going on! They just headed east. Why don't we follow them?

choices.text: Maybe the three of them were putting on an act?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Are you saying they're in this together? But they're already long gone at this point! If they did that to trick us...

talks.objective: Look for the Treasure Hoarders and the redhead

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There they are! Let's find a place to hide and observe.

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: Here are the goods that we agreed upon. It's not much, but it should be enough to help you muddle through for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: Lemme check... Heh, the exact amount you promised. No more, no less.

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: You're not one for flim-flam. We respect that.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'm sure this is just a drop in the ocean for you, and you wouldn't mind if we took a little more, right?

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: I mean, you've got so much Mora that you don't think twice about parting with it. We'll do a better job looking after your fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Seemingly Craven Redhead
dialogues.text: *sigh* I was holding out hope that things would be different this time, but it always ends the same, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: Old tricks are what they are for a reason. If it ain't broke, don't fix it.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: I wonder, are you just as generous when begging for mercy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do you say, {NICKNAME}? Should we help him out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's keep watching for a while.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh? But... Well, you're the boss.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The redhead whistles, and two men leap out from a hidden spot in the woods.

dialogues.speaker: Redhead
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not. You see, we, too, have a few tried-and-true methods to get back everything you've filched from innocent people.

dialogues.speaker: Blond Man
dialogues.text: This is your last chance. Give yourselves up, and you'll save us the trouble of having to go through this whole song and dance.

dialogues.speaker: Brunette Man
dialogues.text: If you ever want a lesson taught, I'm always ready.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: Ha? Where did you two come from? And you... When did you get changed!?

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: Hah, you're the real circus, aren't you? Get ready to be clowned on!

talks.objective: Help the redhead, or watch events unfold

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: You're ganging up on us!

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: This ain't hardly fair.

dialogues.speaker: Bleu
dialogues.text: Boss, what should we do with them?

dialogues.speaker: Redhead
dialogues.text: Why not ask our friends over there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you guys robbers as well?

dialogues.speaker: Redhead
dialogues.text: Oh, that's a toughie. Yes and no.

dialogues.speaker: Blanc
dialogues.text: We only target bad guys, like these two here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not sure Paimon entirely follows, but what Paimon does know is that these two are bad guys. They tried to rob us earlier!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After that, you said that you'd give them valuable cargo for free, and lured the bad guys here into an ambush!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That means you and the other two must be...

response.speaker: Jingle
response.text: Lapdogs of the Maison Gardiennage? Pfft. You make me sick.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Unfortunately for me, that's not the case. I don't agree with the things they do in pursuit of justice... but at least it is justice that they're after.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: That's something you lying good-for-nothings could never understand.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Anyway, we're just a bunch of nobodies, but even nobodies have the right to believe in a cause, especially when it concerns matters of justice. There's no way we'd turn a blind eye to transgressions happening right in front of us.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: They have committed terrible crimes here. And even though they promised to let you walk free, they never intended to actually let that happen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How do you know what they're actually thinking?

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: You must listen carefully, not only with your ears, but with your head, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Speaking of which, Penny did say...)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You take a few deep breaths to cast aside a few unwanted thoughts and clear your head.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Try to recall what they said.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: "All that for some{RUBY#[D]What an idiot!}one you've never met... You have a heart {RUBY#[D]If your heart was real gold, then we'd be in business.}of gold, my friend! I'm so {RUBY#[D]Gold or not, I'm gonna rip it right out.}touched."

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: #"We are men {RUBY#[D]As if verbal agreements amount to anything.}of our word. We'll let you walk free today, {M#bro}{F#girl}{RUBY#[D]We'll be back to finish you once we're done with this moron.}, and take your pet with you!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You, scared? Paimon's not buying it for a second.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's seen this all before. Bad guys never change, and words take on different meanings once you process them.

response.speaker: Jingle
response.text: What do you mean "what we a{RUBY#[D]They must be bluffing.}ctually think"... We say what{RUBY#[D]I'm not gonna fall for this.} we mean! It's {RUBY#[D]Nope!}true!

response.speaker: Havisham
response.text: We just got carried away, that's all. {RUBY#[D]Well, maybe once or twice. Three times?} This has never happened before. We've learned {RUBY#[D]We've got to get backup.}our lesson!

response.speaker: Jingle
response.text: Here, take our loot{RUBY#[D]Most of our stuff is back at camp.}. It's all yours. Life has not {RUBY#[D](bad luck running into this lot)}been kind to us, or else we would never have{RUBY#[D]We'd better warn the others.} stooped as low as robbing.

response.speaker: Havisham
response.text: Please give us another chance! We'll {RUBY#[D]Once we're back at camp, we'll get the others. You're gonna pay!}make an honest living in Lumidouce Harbor.

response.speaker: Jingle
response.text: Of co{RUBY#[D]As if...}urse.

response.speaker: Havisham
response.text: As we {RUBY#[D]They sound delusional}have said, so have {RUBY#[D]But that makes things easier}you heard.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Okay, then. We'll believe you once more. Bleu, Blanc, let them go.

response.speaker: Blanc
response.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Jingle
response.text: We promise to {RUBY#[D]Call for backup}become better men.

response.speaker: Havisham
response.text: And we will thank you {RUBY#[D]with some broken ribs}properly in the future!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Having said their piece, the two Treasure Hoarders hurriedly head south.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How could you let them go? Paimon's sure you heard their thoughts as clearly as we did.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: What's the hurry? Since you heard their thoughts, you must be aware that not only do they plan to continue with their crimes, but that they also have plenty of accomplices.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you're playing the long game.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Bingo. This is the perfect opportunity for all the fish to swim into our net. I'd be an idiot to let this slip by.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But what if there are too many of them? Can we come with you? {NICKNAME} knows a few moves.

choices.text: If you hadn't led them away in the first place...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you had saved this guy, their master plan would have been foiled!

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Since you're willing to help, I'll give Bleu and Blanc a day off.

response.speaker: Blanc
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Bleu
response.text: Fine with me. The boss calls the shots.

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Those two lying weasels have returned to their camp to rally their brethren. Let's give them some time, then pay a visit tomorrow evening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem. By the way, we still don't know your name.

response.speaker: Rouge
response.text: Name? It's just a codename, but you may call me Rouge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rouge... We've heard that name before, from Penny! Now that Paimon thinks of it, it did sound oddly familiar when you were going on about listening with your head.

response.speaker: Rouge
response.text: You know Penny? She's spoken to you about me? What a coincidence.

response.speaker: Rouge
response.text: Small world we live in...

choices.text: Robbing bad guys every now and then is a hobby of mine as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's sure you meant to say "punishing," right?

choices.text: Someone even worse than the bad guys!

response.speaker: Redhead
response.text: Haha! If you want to teach unsavory characters a lesson, you must become yet more unsavory. Looks like you already know that.

talks.objective: Go to the Treasure Hoarder camp

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: There's some cargo here. It looks like the gang has been busy... but I think they'll take the hint this time around.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Since you've done your part, you should have some of these as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It feels weird... I'll pass.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Suit yourself. Thank you anyway! I fear I don't have anything else to offer you except my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you gonna do with the loot?

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Give to those in need, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Oh, I get it now. You thought I was gonna keep this all to myself. If I were to do that, I'd be no different from them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, like, what do you really plan to do?

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: I meant what I said to Havisham and Jingle. I'm sure you know that by now.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: The world is full of extreme inequity, poverty, and greed.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Some people resort to a life of crime only because they have encountered difficulties that they believe are insurmountable. I would love to lend those people a hand.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Havisham and Jingle, on the other hand, belong to the other group: those marred by insatiable greed, who resort to violence to rob the weak and seize what doesn't belong to them.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: If the laws of Fontaine cannot ensure that they receive the punishment they deserve, then I will. Whatever your opinion, I will continue doing what I believe to be the right thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure you have your reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: You could call this arrogance, which in turn could be construed as another form of greed.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Fortunately, I'm not alone on this path, and there are like-minded people by my side. Even if we can make just a tiny difference in the world...

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Thanks all the same! Farewell!

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: You're ganging up on us!

dialogues.speaker: Havisham
dialogues.text: This ain't hardly fair.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: It's almost time. Let's set out for the Treasure Hoarder hideout in the south.

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: So we meet again! Didn't you say you had a gift for us? Some broken ribs, if I recall correctly? I appreciate the sentiment, but I personally think that's a present that suits you far better.

dialogues.speaker: Jingle
dialogues.text: You liar! You never intended on letting us go!

dialogues.speaker: Rouge
dialogues.text: Well, I would say the same to you!
